name: residue-kind-not-just-size
description: A named residue can be the wrong KIND of statement, not merely mispriced — "a computation about specific morphisms" was three lemma calls, and the real obligation was a covering property nobody had named

A handoff that names its residue precisely ("the Gal-coproduct's γ-component
inclusion composed with the two projections gives id and γ — a computation about
specific morphisms, not a missing lemma") and lists its ingredients
(`pullbackSpecIso`, `IsIso (sigmaSpec …)`, `galoisSelfTensorEquiv`) can still be
wrong about **what kind of statement** is owed. All three ingredients were needed
for none of it: the section came from `pullback.lift` and the two identities were
`pullback.lift_fst`/`lift_snd`. The real obligation was one level up and a
different kind of fact — that the γ-indexed section family **covers** the
self-pullback.

**Why:** a precise-sounding residue gets inherited verbatim. Two sites and a board
row carried this one, and the summary list even attached a plausible blocker
("sticks on `Scheme.Spec.map` versus `Spec.map`"), which is exactly what makes a
reader believe it was attempted. Nothing in a sorry sweep, axiom check, or
vacuity sweep reads a residue paragraph.

**How to apply:** before paying a named residue, write the statement it describes
and try to *construct* it from the universal properties already in scope — do not
start from its ingredient list. If it falls out, ask what the ingredients were
actually for; that answer is usually the real obligation, and it is often a
different kind of statement (a covering, a finiteness, an inhabitation) rather
than a harder version of the same one. Then check whether the two directions of
the bridge are symmetric: [[opposite-monotonicity-is-not-separability]] is the
same shape one layer down. Related: [[reprice-the-prescription-before-paying-it]],
[[price-the-proof-term-not-the-statement]], [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]].

Corollary found the same session: when the free direction turns out
unconditional, the *binder list* stops being where the hypothesis lives. Neither
implication here carries `IsGalois`; the Galois hypothesis sits in an explicit
antecedent. A lane auditing binders per [[qualified-binder-hides-from-census]]
would report "no Galois dependence" and be wrong about the route.
